1.4.501: FUND CREATED; ADMINISTRATION:
   A.   There is hereby created the police pension fund. The fund shall be
administered by a Board that shall consist of the Mayor or designee, the Chief
of Police, Chief Financial Officer, and two (2) active or retired members of
the police pension plan. The Board shall be designated the "Police Pension Fund
Board".
   B.   An active or retired member of the police pension fund shall be elected
annually to the Police Pension Fund Board for a term of two (2) years.
Initially, two (2) members of the Police Pension Fund Board shall be elected,
one for a two (2) year term and one for a one year term, so that annually
thereafter one member shall be elected for a two (2) year term.
   C.   The City Attorney shall advise and represent the Board in all matters
pertaining to its duties and the management of the fund whenever required.
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.502: RESERVED:
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.503: RESERVED:
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.504: BOARD TRUSTEE OF FUNDS; REPORT:
The Police Pension Fund Board shall be the trustee of all monies, securities
and other property belonging to the fund and, at the last meeting of the City
Council in August of each year, shall report to the City Council as to the
condition of the fund. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.505: DISPOSITION OF MONIES:
   A.   Monies Not Transferred: Monies remaining at the end of any fiscal year
in the fund shall not be transferred to any other fund.
   B.   Investment Of Funds: The police pension fund shall be invested only in
bonds, warrants, securities, obligations and other investments or deposits or
accounts as may be from time to time authorized by law and as determined and
approved by the Board. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.506: RECIPIENTS OF BENEFITS:
A person who is a regularly employed member of the Police Department of the
City under the classified civil service, who was sworn into duty on or before
April 7, 1978, and who is not a member of any other plan maintained by or for
the City for regularly employed members of the Police Department under the
classified civil service, is a member of the plan specified in this part. (Ord.
11-18)
1.4.507: SOURCES OF REVENUE FOR THE FUND:
   A.   Each member shall pay into the fund monthly ten percent (10%) of the
base salary, longevity pay, additional pay based on length of service and
performance pay, if any, paid to the member. The payment shall be made by the
employer by deduction from the salary paid and the contribution so picked up
shall be treated as employer contributions pursuant to section 414(h)(2) of the
Internal Revenue Code as amended and Colorado Revised Statutes section 31-31-
407. The employer shall pay these employee contributions directly to the Fire
and Police Pension Association as created by Colorado Revised Statutes section
31-31-201, and not to the member. The contributions shall be paid from the same
funds that are used to pay salaries to the employees. The contributions,
although designated as employee contributions, shall be paid by the employer in
lieu of contributions by employees. Employees may not elect to choose to
receive the contributions directly instead of having them paid by the employer
to the pension plan. Employee contributions so picked up shall be treated for
all purposes of this section in the same manner as employee contributions made
before the date picked up. All payments shall be credited to the pension fund.
   B.   Until December 31, 2013, if the difference, as determined by an
actuarial valuation, between the annual amount necessary to pay plan normal
costs and amortize unfunded actuarial accrued liability, and the annual
contributions from the employee and employer, is one hundred thirty thousand
dollars ($130,000.00) or less, that difference, in an amount not to exceed one
hundred thirty thousand dollars ($130,000.00), of available, annual proceeds
from the sale of unclaimed property only, shall be paid to the police pension
plan. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.508: RETIREMENT PENSION:
   A.   Any member of the Police Department who is a member of this police
pension fund and who shall have served twenty five (25) years or more of active
duty and shall have attained the age of fifty (50) years, shall be retired
within thirty (30) days after making application for retirement, except during
periods of national emergency, and the person shall be paid a monthly pension
equal to one-half (1/2) the amount of the final monthly base salary, one-half
(1/2) longevity pay, and one-half (1/2) of additional pay based on length of
service the person received as a member of the Department as of the date of
application for retirement. For so long as the member of the Department is in
retirement, there shall be added to the amount of the pension as stated above,
one-half (1/2) of any increase in base salary and longevity or additional pay
based on length of service granted to the rank formerly occupied by the member
in the Department. Monthly base salary as used in this subsection shall not
include proficiency pay, merit pay, special assignment pay, or any other extra
pay, however denominated.
   B.   Any member or former member of the Department, who on the effective
date hereof is receiving a pension or annuity from the fund by reason of
retirement, shall likewise receive a monthly pension or annuity from the fund
equal to one-half (1/2) of the current monthly base salary paid to the rank the
member occupied on the date of retirement plus one-half (1/2) of all longevity
or additional pay which would have accrued to any member by reason of similar
length of service in the Police Department under any pertinent longevity or
additional pay provision currently in effect in the City, plus one-half (1/2)
of any increase in base salary and longevity or additional pay based on length
of service granted during the period of retirement to the rank occupied in the
Department. The pension shall continue to be paid as long as the member is in
retirement.
   C.   In addition to the pension benefit described in subsections A and B of
this section and as long as the member remains in retirement, there shall be
added one-half (1/2) of the amount of annual performance pay awarded, if any,
to all sworn members of the Department for the preceding year. The total annual
performance pay amount paid to eligible, active, sworn members of the
Department shall be expressed as a percentage of total salaries paid to all
sworn members of the Department and the pension benefit amount for each retiree
shall be increased by the same percentage amount.
   D.   For purposes of this part the following terms shall be defined as
follows:
ADDITIONAL PAY BASED ON LENGTH OF SERVICE: Pay based upon up to forty (40)
hours per year for vacation sellback at the current rate of pay according to
the rank of the member at the time of retirement together with any other
compensation to which the member is entitled based upon longevity and from
which a pension contribution has been taken from the member.
LONGEVITY PAY: Twenty dollars ($20.00) if the member has completed five (5)
years of service, plus four dollars ($4.00) for each year of service after five
(5) years, but not more than one hundred dollars ($100.00). (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.509: BENEFITS WHEN FORMER CLASSIFIED CIVIL SERVICE RANK ABOLISHED:
When for any reason a classified civil service rank or grade within the Police
Department is abolished or ceases to exist then any member of the Department
who is in receipt of a pension or annuity from the fund by reason of retirement
in the classification, grade or rank and any member of the Department who may
be retired in the future in the classification, grade or rank shall receive
pension benefits equal to one-half (1/2) of the "median base salary" between
the next higher and the next lower rank or grade. To one-half (1/2) of this
"median base salary" shall be added one-half (1/2) of any longevity pay which
was paid to the member at the time of retirement, plus one-half (1/2) of any
additional pay based upon length of service. A member of the Department who is
in receipt of a pension or annuity from the fund by reason of retirement in a
classified civil service rank or grade which has been abolished or has ceased
to exist, shall have the member's benefits, as above described, recomputed from
January 1, 1993, and any additional monies to which the member is entitled
shall be paid to the member as if this provision were in effect at that date.
Following is an example on how the retirement pay for an abolished rank will be
calculated:
 
HBS                       = Next higher rank base salary
LBS                       = Next lower rank base salary
L                         = Longevity
ALS                       = Additional pay based on length of service
MBS                       = Median base salary
(HBS)+(LBS)               = MBS
2
1/2 MBS + 1/2 L + 1/2 ALS = Retirement pay for abolished position
 
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.510: DISABILITY BENEFITS:
   A.   Disability Incurred On Duty:
      1.   Any member of the Police Department who while in the performance of
assigned duties becomes permanently disabled from any cause not intentionally
self-inflicted nor due to habitual use of intoxicants or drugs, resulting in
permanent incapacity to perform assigned duties, shall be retired by the Board.
Any member of the Police Department who has completed five (5) years or more as
a member of the Department, but who is unable to perform duties by reason of
heart disease shall be presumed, unless the presumption is overcome by
competent evidence, to have contracted the disease while on active duty as a
result of strain and shall be retired by the Board.
      2.   In cases where a special position or assignment can or may be
assigned to the member, the member may be assigned to the special position or
assignment. Any retirement shall be for the period of the disability and no
longer.
      3.   Members, whether now or hereafter retired under this section, shall
be paid a monthly pension equal to one-half (1/2) the amount of the member's
monthly salary and longevity pay as of the date of retirement plus one-half (1/
2) of any increase in salary and longevity or additional pay based on length of
service granted during the period of retirement to the rank occupied in the
Department. The retired member, after retirement, shall continue to accrue
longevity and length of service shall continue to extend in the same manner and
with the same limitations as if the retired member was still active and not
retired. The pension shall continue to be paid as long as the member is in
retirement.
      4.   All applicants for disability pensions shall be examined by one or
more physicians selected for the purpose by the Board, and may be examined by
one or more physicians selected by the applicant. All expenses of examination
by the physician chosen by the Board shall be paid by the Board out of the
fund.
      5.   The Board shall establish the general rules and regulations as it
deems proper for the purpose of reexamination of all persons who have been
retired for disability or who may be so retired hereafter to determine from
time to time the fitness of the persons to return to active duty in the
Department. No person who has reached the age of fifty (50) years either before
or after retirement shall be reexamined. No person who has completed twenty
five (25) years of active duty in the Department before the date of retirement
shall be reexamined. No person on the retired list shall be examined sooner
than one year after date of retirement and not more frequently than once a year
thereafter. In the event it is found by the Board that any member on the
retired list has recovered from the disability which caused the member
retirement, if the person is under fifty (50) years of age and has served less
than twenty five (25) years of active duty shall be removed from the retired
list and ordered to report to the chief officer of the Department within thirty
(30) days for assignment to active duty. During the period of thirty (30) days,
the member may file a written protest in which the member shall state any
objection that the member may have to be removed from the retired list. The
decision of the Board shall be suspended pending a hearing on the protest, at
which hearing the member shall have a right to appear and to be represented by
counsel. During the period that any member is ordered retired for disability by
the Board, the member if under the age of fifty (50) years and having served
less than twenty five (25) years of active duty shall be carried on a special
roll of the Police Department and listed as inactive.
   B.   Disability Incurred Off Duty: Any member of the Police Department who
is found to be permanently and totally disabled by injuries not received while
on assigned duties in the Police Department shall be paid so long as the
disability shall last according to the following formula: two and one-half
percent (21/2%) of the monthly salary and longevity pay multiplied by the
number of years of service already credited, to a maximum of fifty percent
(50%) of the monthly salary and longevity pay being received at the time of
disability. There shall be added to the benefit two and one-half percent (21/
2%) of any increase in salary and longevity pay granted during the period of
retirement to the rank occupied by the member in the Department multiplied by
the number of years of service credited at the time of disability, but in no
event shall the member receive in excess of fifty percent (50%) of any salary
and longevity pay increase; provided, however, that when a member is disabled
off duty during employment with another employer and is receiving payments
under workers' compensation or any other compensatory plan provided by the
employer with respect to the injury, the member's disability pension from the
City shall abate to the extent of the other disability compensation which is
furnished by the other employer. The provisions covering examinations and
reexaminations as set forth in subsection A of this section shall be applicable
to all cases arising under this subsection. No disability payments shall be
payable where the disability is intentionally self-inflicted or due to the
habitual use of intoxicants or drugs.
   C.   Commencement Of Benefits: The benefits provided in subsections A and B
of this section shall commence immediately and accrued sick leave shall be
compensated as provided elsewhere in this chapter.
   D.   Application: The provisions of this section were superseded by State
statute effective January 1, 1980, and do not apply for benefits received after
that date. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.511: BENEFITS TO DEPENDENTS:
   A.   Death In Service:
      1.   If any member of the Police Department shall die while in service
and having reached eligibility for normal retirement, and shall leave a spouse
but no children, the spouse shall receive from the departmental pension fund
one-third (1/3) of the monthly salary and longevity pay or additional pay based
on length of service the member received at the time of the member's death or
one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) per month, whichever is greater. The
spouse's pension shall be computed in the same manner and subject to the same
options as would have been available to the member and shall also be subject to
increases computed in the same manner as for the member's pensions under this
chapter, except that a spouse shall receive one-third (1/3) of any increase
rather than one-half (1/2).
      2.   Where the member at the time of death is survived by a spouse and a
child or children under eighteen (18) years of age, or twenty three (23) if
unmarried and enrolled as a full time student in an accredited institution of
higher learning, there shall be paid to each child thirty dollars ($30.00)
monthly in addition to the spouse's pension; where there is no spouse surviving
but there are children under age eighteen (18), or twenty three (23) if
unmarried and enrolled as a full time student in an accredited institution of
higher learning, then the spouse's pension provided hereunder shall be prorated
among the child or children or they shall receive thirty dollars ($30.00)
monthly each, whichever is greater.
   B.   Death After Retirement:
      1.   The surviving spouse of a member who was receiving a monthly pension
shall receive one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) monthly or two-thirds (2/3)
of the member's total monthly pension, whichever is greater. The spouse's
pension provided by this part shall be increased in proportion to any increase
in members' pensions under sections
1.4.508,
1.4.509 and
1.4.512 of this part. For purposes of this subsection, the term "spouse" means
the spouse of the member on the date of retirement.
      2.   Where the member at the time of death is survived by a spouse and a
child or children, there shall be paid to each child thirty dollars ($30.00)
monthly; where there is no spouse surviving but there are children under age
eighteen (18), or twenty three (23) if unmarried and enrolled as a full time
student in an accredited institution of higher learning, then the spouse's
pension shall be prorated among the child or children or they shall receive
thirty dollars ($30.00) monthly each, whichever is greater. For purposes of
this section, the term "spouse" means the spouse of the member on the date of
retirement.
   C.   Limitation On Benefits For Surviving Children: All benefits provided
under this section for surviving children shall terminate upon the eighteenth
birthday of any surviving child, or age twenty three (23) if unmarried and
enrolled as a full time student in an accredited institution of higher
learning.
   D.   Optional Survivor's Benefit For A Spouse From A Postretirement
Marriage:
      1.   A member who marries after retirement may make a lifetime election
of one of the following reduced pensions:
         a.   A monthly pension for life and upon the death of the member, a
monthly pension of sixty seven percent (67%) of that reduced monthly pension
payable to the surviving spouse for life.
         b.   A monthly pension for life and upon the death of the member, a
monthly pension of sixty seven percent (67%) of that reduced monthly pension
payable to the surviving spouse for life. If the marriage is terminated by the
death of the spouse or by a decree of dissolution, the monthly pension payable
to the member shall be increased to the preelection amount, and there will be
no survivor benefit.
         c.   A monthly pension for life and upon the death of the member, a
monthly pension of thirty three percent (33%) of that reduced monthly pension
payable to the surviving spouse for life.
         d.   A monthly pension for life and upon the death of the member, a
monthly pension of thirty three percent (33%) of that reduced monthly pension
payable to the surviving spouse for life. If the marriage is terminated by the
death of the spouse or by a decree of dissolution, the monthly pension payable
to the member shall be increased to the preelection amount, and there will be
no survivor benefit.
      2.   The reduced pension shall be an amount that is actuarially equal to
the pension that was paid or would have been payable to the member prior to the
election, as determined by a certified actuary.
      3.   The election must be in writing and must be submitted not later than
one hundred eighty (180) days after the marriage of the member. The election is
irrevocable. If within one hundred eighty (180) days of the date of the
election the member dies or the marriage is dissolved, the election is void.
Amounts payable under a domestic relations order (DRO) will not be affected by
this election. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.512: RETURN OF CONTRIBUTIONS; VESTED RIGHTS; SUPPLEMENTAL RETIREMENT
PENSION:
   A.   Whenever any member shall terminate employment with the Police
Department for reasons other than death or retirement, total contributions due
to date of termination shall be returned to the member without interest;
provided, however, that any member having twenty (20) or more years' credited
service may leave their contribution and upon reaching the age of fifty (50)
years shall receive a pension equal to two percent (2%) per year for each full
year of credited service, but not to exceed one-half (1/2) the amount of the
member's final monthly base salary. Any member making this election shall not
receive the rank escalation benefit for the period between termination and upon
reaching the age of fifty (50) years and all postmedical benefits shall be
terminated indefinitely, unless the member begins receiving benefit payments
immediately upon termination of employment and then all postmedical benefits
shall be retained. In the event that an inactive member who is eligible for
vested benefits dies prior to the commencement of the member's benefit
payments, the surviving spouse and surviving children shall start receiving
dependent benefits according to subsections
1.4.511B and C of this part at the time when the member would have reached the
age of fifty (50) years. If a member who has started receiving vested benefit
payments dies, the benefit payments will continue.
   B.   Upon reaching eligibility for normal retirement (as defined in
subsection
1.4.508A of this part), employee contributions, as described in subsection
1.4.507A of this part, made by a member of the police pension fund subsequent
to reaching eligibility for normal retirement, shall be credited to a
supplemental retirement account established in the member's name. At the time
the member is granted a normal retirement and provided that the member has
remained a member of this police pension fund for a minimum of twenty four (24)
months beyond reaching eligibility for normal retirement, contributions
credited to this supplemental retirement account, together with investment
earnings or losses, if any, shall be returned to the member in accord with
available payment options as determined by the City in accord with applicable
Internal Revenue Service requirements. No contributions will be credited to any
member's supplemental retirement account prior to January 1, 1996.
   C.   Administration of these supplemental retirement accounts shall be
accomplished in accord with rules 304.01 through 304.08, of the Colorado Fire
and Police Pension Association Rules and Regulations as codified November 18,
1997.
   D.   In addition to the regular retirement pension defined in subsection
1.4.508A of this part, and at the member's option, in lieu of the supplemental
retirement account benefit defined in subsection B of this section, any member
who retires on or after July 1, 1998, after having served at least one full
year beyond eligibility for normal retirement as defined in subsection
1.4.508A of this part, shall be eligible to receive a monthly supplemental
retirement pension upon retirement from active duty. This supplemental
retirement benefit shall be equal to three percent (3%) of the current monthly
base salary plus three percent (3%) of the longevity pay and other additional
pay based upon length of service paid to the rank the member occupied on the
date of retirement for each full year of active service completed after
reaching normal retirement eligibility, up to a maximum of six (6) years of
additional service or eighteen percent (18%) of base salary and longevity pay
and additional pay based upon length of service. Provided, however, no
eligibility shall accrue for the supplemental retirement pension for having
served beyond eligibility for normal retirement in the period prior to January
1, 1996.
This supplemental retirement pension shall be increased annually, proportionate
to the current active duty base salary in a manner similar to any increase
computed for member's normal retirement pension and as described in section
1.4.508 of this part. If the rank the member occupied at the time of retirement
is subsequently abolished, the supplemental retirement pension shall be
calculated based upon the average of the salary of the next higher and next
lower ranks.
In order to receive the supplemental retirement pension, a member must formally
waive any right to any and all monies contained in a supplemental retirement
account as provided in subsection B of this section. This waiver shall be made
at the time of retirement. Any member who fails to make this waiver shall
retain rights to any monies in his/her supplemental retirement account but
shall be forever barred from receiving the supplemental retirement pension.
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.513: COUNCIL MAY CHANGE, REPEAL PROVISIONS:
The Council shall have power at any time to change or repeal any of the
provisions of this part including those prescribing the terms, conditions and
amounts to be paid to or from the fund, notwithstanding service in the
Department, or donation or payment into the fund of any amount by the officer,
member or employee or any other person. Any increase or decrease in the amount
of benefits payable under this part shall be made as the Council shall deem
necessary to accord with changing financial and economic conditions; provided,
that no pensioner whose rights are vested shall be paid less than the amount of
the pension originally paid upon attainment of eligibility for benefits, and
provided further that the percentage of members' contribution under this plan
shall never exceed the percentage of contributions to pension plans made by
employees of City departments other than police and fire. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.514: WORK HOURS, SICK LEAVE BENEFITS NOT AFFECTED:
This part shall not be construed to repeal work hours, sick leave or other
fringe benefits provided elsewhere in this chapter, nor to affect any rights
already vested. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.515: BENEFITS, REGULATIONS OF:
   A.   Benefits Prorated When Funds Insufficient To Pay In Full: If at any
time the money, security and other property to the credit of the fund be
insufficient to make the monthly payments accruing hereunder, then the
beneficiaries shall equally prorate the funds until the time as the condition
of the fund warrants the payment of their benefits in full. Arrearages of
benefits for one year may be paid in any future year and shall enter into and
form part of the basis of distribution for the year but shall not otherwise be
preferred.
   B.   Benefits Not Subject To Levy Or Attachment: No portion of the fund
shall before or after its order for distribution be held, seized, taken or
subjected to or detained, or levied upon by virtue of any attachment,
execution, writ, interlocutory, or other order or decree or any process or
proceeding whatever issued out of or by any court in this or any other state,
for the payment or satisfaction, in whole or part, of any debt, claim, demand
or judgment against any beneficiary of the fund, but the fund shall be held and
distributed for the purpose of this part and for no other purpose whatever.
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.516: TEMPORARY APPOINTMENTS:
Whenever a temporary appointment is made to the Police Department under the
rules of the Civil Service Commission, no deduction shall be made from the
salary of the temporary appointee for the police pension fund and the temporary
appointee shall receive no benefits or payments from the fund and shall have no
claim against the fund. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.517: DEFERRED RETIREMENT OPTION PLAN:
   A.   Establishment; Citation; Purpose:
      1.   This section adds an optional account known as the deferred
retirement option plan.
      2.   The provisions of this section may be cited as the "DROP".
      3.   The purpose of the DROP is to allow an eligible member to elect in
lieu of immediate termination of employment and receipt of a service retirement
benefit, to continue employment for a specified period of time and to have the
member's employee contribution, plus the retirement benefits the member would
receive if employment terminated, paid into the DROP account until the end of
the specified period of participation, at which time employment is to cease.
   B.   Eligibility For Participation; Limitations:
      1.   Participation in the DROP is an option available to any member of
the police pension fund who is eligible to retire in accord with section
1.4.508 of this part.
      2.   A member may participate in DROP only once.
      3.   The duration of a member's participation in the DROP shall not
exceed a total of five (5) years. As a condition precedent to participation in
DROP, the member shall execute an irrevocable agreement with the Police Pension
Fund Board and the City of Colorado Springs, which agreement shall, among other
items, clearly and unequivocally state that the member must retire no later
than the fifth anniversary of initial participation in DROP. The member shall
also acknowledge that no disbursement of DROP funds can occur absent the
retirement or death of the member.
      4.   If the member's participation in the DROP is interrupted by: a)
military service, b) reduction in work force, or c) job related disability,
upon reestablishment of membership, provided the member has not received any
distribution from the member's DROP account, the member shall be immediately
eligible for resumption of participation for the balance of the five (5) year
maximum. Other than the above described types of interruptions, the five (5)
year period shall continue to run in all other cases.
   C.   Conditions Of Participation; Effects:
      1.   Upon commencement of participation in the DROP, the member shall
remain an active member. Nevertheless, the member shall earn no additional
service credit and the pension benefit described in subsections
1.4.508A, B and C of this part shall be established and calculated in accord
with the rules contained in that section.
      2.   Upon commencement of participation, the retirement pension benefits
described in subsection
1.4.507A of this part shall be paid into the deferred retirement option plan
account. In no case shall the employer contribution be used to fund the DROP.
      3.   The deferred retirement option plan assets shall be held in trust
for investment purposes as part of the fire and police members' self-directed
investments fund, subject to such rules as may be adopted for the
administration of the trust. The FPPA Board shall be authorized to charge each
account a reasonable fee for the administration of the DROP.
      4.   The deferred retirement option plan account shall not be subject to
any fees or charges of any kind for any purpose, except as otherwise agreed by
the City and FPPA.
   D.   Payments To Member:
      1.   A member in the DROP who terminates employment or reaches the five
(5) year limit for participation shall become a retiree and shall be entitled
to select one of the following distribution methods:
         a.   Deferral of any payment(s) from the account until a specified
date. If a deferral of payment(s) is selected, the member shall select one of
the following distribution methods. However, all distributions must start no
later than the year in which the member attains the age of seventy and one-half
(701/2).
         b.   A lump sum distribution of the entire account balance.
         c.   Periodic monthly payments with a designated amount until the
balance of the DROP account has been entirely distributed.
         d.   Periodic payments for a designated period of years. FPPA will
calculate the dollar amount of the member's periodic payment, so that the
entire balance in the member's DROP account will have been distributed to the
member by the end of the period selected by the member. This amount will be
recalculated annually during April.
         e.   Initial minimum required distribution. The FPPA will calculate
the dollar amount of the member's periodic payment based on the member's
current DROP account balance. The minimum distribution is based on the member's
life expectancy (and the life expectancy of the member's designated
beneficiary, if applicable).
         f.   Combination of lump sum and periodic payments by designating an
initial lump sum payment of a specified amount and a balance to be paid in a
specified number of monthly payments of a specified dollar amount until the
balance of the DROP account has been entirely distributed to the member.
      2.   Regardless of the form of payment the member chooses, the minimum
distribution amount will be determined and made in accord with Internal Revenue
Code section 401(a)(9) and the regulations thereunder, including the minimum
distribution incidental death benefit requirement. If no selection is made by
the retiree within thirty (30) days of retirement, the lump sum payment method
shall be utilized.
   E.   Payments To Beneficiaries:
      1.   The legal spouse of a member shall be the primary beneficiary of the
DROP account for the purpose of survivor benefits. If a member is not legally
married, the member may elect one or more primary beneficiaries to receive the
balance of the account in the event of the member's death. A member may also
elect one or more contingent beneficiaries who would be eligible to receive the
proceeds of the DROP account in the event that no primary beneficiary survives
the member by at least thirty (30) days.
      2.   The member may change elective beneficiaries as personal
circumstances dictate.
      3.   If a member dies during the period of participation in the DROP plan
and the legal spouse of the member is the beneficiary, at the spouse's option,
the member shall be eligible to receive either: a) a lump sum payment equal to
the account balance plus any accrued interest, or b) equal monthly installment
payments from the member's individual DROP account over a period of no more
than ten (10) years. If the beneficiary is other than the spouse of the member
or if no selection is made by the spouse beneficiary within thirty (30) days of
death of the member, the lump sum payment method shall be utilized.
      4.   In the event that the member dies and is not survived by a
designated beneficiary by at least thirty (30) days, the member's estate shall
receive a lump sum payment equal to the member's individual DROP account
balance, plus any accrued interest.
      5.   Payments of DROP account proceeds shall be in addition to other
normal survivor benefits payable to survivors of retirees as provided in this
article.
   F.   Compliance With IRS Requirements: The Board shall take all necessary
steps to ensure that the DROP is administered in full compliance with all
applicable IRS rules, regulations and determinations. For purposes of the
limits of Internal Revenue Code section 415, the DROP is considered a defined
benefit plan to which the ninety thousand dollar ($90,000.00) limit of Internal
Revenue Code section 415(b) (as adjusted for cost of living changes under
Internal Revenue Code section 415(d) and as applicable to governmental police
plans) applies at the time benefits are paid from the DROP plan. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.518: DIRECT ROLLOVERS:
For distributions made on or after January 1, 1993, a member or beneficiary may
elect, at the time and in the manner prescribed by the Police Pension Fund
Board, to have any portion of an eligible rollover distribution paid directly
to an eligible retirement plan specified by the member or beneficiary in a
direct rollover. For purposes of applying this section, the following
definitions shall apply:
DISTRIBUTEE: Includes an employee or former employee. In addition, the
employee's or former employee's surviving spouse and the employee's or former
employee's spouse or former spouse who is the alternative payee under a
qualified domestic relations order, as defined in Internal Revenue Code section
414(p), are distributees with regard to the interest of the spouse or former
spouse.
ELIGIBLE RETIREMENT PLAN: An individual retirement account described in
Internal Revenue Code section 408(a), an individual retirement annuity
described in Internal Revenue Code section 408(b), an annuity plan described in
Internal Revenue Code section 403(a) that accepts the distributee's eligible
rollover distribution or a qualified trust described in Internal Revenue Code
section 401(a). However, in the case of an eligible rollover distribution to
the surviving spouse, an eligible retirement plan is an individual retirement
account or individual retirement annuity.
ELIGIBLE ROLLOVER DISTRIBUTION: Any distribution of all or any portion of the
balance to the credit of the distributee, except that an eligible rollover
distribution does not include any distribution that is one of a series of
substantially equal periodic payments (not less frequently than annually) made
for the life (or life expectancy) of the distributee or the joint lives (or
joint life expectancies) of the distributee and the distributee's designated
beneficiary, or for a specified period of ten (10) years or more; any
distribution to the extent the distribution is required under Internal Revenue
Code section 401(a)(9); and the portion of any distribution that is not
includable in gross income.
Effective January 1, 2002, an eligible retirement plan shall also mean an
annuity contract described in Internal Revenue Code section 403(b) and an
eligible plan under Internal Revenue Code section 457(b) that is maintained by
a state, political subdivision of a state, or agency or instrumentality of a
state or political subdivision of a state and that agrees separately to account
for amounts transferred into the plan from this plan. The definition of
eligible retirement plan shall also apply in the case of a distribution to a
surviving spouse, or to a spouse or former spouse who is the alternate payee
under a qualified domestic relations order, as defined in Internal Revenue Code
section 414(p).
For distributions on or after January 1, 2002, a portion of distribution shall
not fail to be an eligible rollover distribution merely because the portion
consists of after tax employee contributions that are not includable in gross
income. However, that portion may be paid only to an individual retirement
account or annuity described in section 408(a) or (b) of the Internal Revenue
Code, or to a qualified defined contribution plan described in section 401(a)
or 403(a) of the Internal Revenue Code that agrees separately to account for
the amounts so transferred, including separately accounting for the portion of
the distribution which is includable in gross income and the portion of the
distribution which is not so includable. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.519: EXCLUSIVE BENEFIT RULE:
All contributions made to the police pension fund shall be used solely for the
exclusive benefit of members and their beneficiaries and to defray reasonable
expenses of the police pension fund. Forfeitures arising because of death or
termination of employment before a member becomes eligible for a benefit from
the plan or arising for any other reason shall be applied to reduce the cost of
the plan, not to increase the benefits otherwise payable to members. (Ord. 11-
18)
1.4.520: INTERNAL REVENUE SERVICE LIMITATIONS:
   A.   Compensation Limits: The compensation taken into account for any
purpose under the police pension fund shall not exceed the applicable amount
under Internal Revenue Code section 401(a)(17) one hundred fifty thousand
dollars ($150,000.00), as adjusted for cost of living changes according to
Internal Revenue Code section 401(a)(17).
   B.   Benefit Limits: The police pension fund is subject to the limitations
on benefits described in Internal Revenue Code section 415(b) for governmental
police plans, which limitations are incorporated herein by this reference.
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.521: LATEST DISTRIBUTION DATE:
Payment of a member's benefit shall commence no later than April 1 of the
calendar year following the later of: a) the calendar year in which the member
attains age seventy and one-half (701/2), or b) the calendar year in which the
member's employment with the Police Department terminates. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.522: VESTING UPON PLAN TERMINATION:
If the police pension plan is terminated, the rights of all affected members to
benefits accrued to the date of the termination, to the extent then funded,
shall be nonforfeitable. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.523: MILITARY SERVICE:
Effective December 12, 1994, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary,
contributions, benefits and service credit with respect to qualified military
service will be provided in accord with Internal Revenue Code section 414(u).
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.524: RULES, FORMS, AND AGREEMENTS:
The Police Pension Fund Board is hereby authorized to promulgate all rules,
forms and agreements necessary for the implementation of sections
1.4.518 through
1.4.523 of this part. (Ord. 11-18)

(Ord. 11-18)

1.4.701: FUND CREATED; ADMINISTRATION:
   A.   There is hereby created the firefighter's pension fund. The fund shall
be administered by a Board that shall consist of the Mayor or designee, the
Fire Chief, the Chief Financial Officer, and two (2) active or retired members
of the fire pension plan. The Board shall be designated the "Fire Pension Fund
Board".
   B.   An active or retired member of the fire pension fund shall be elected
annually to the Fire Pension Fund Board for a term of two (2) years. Initially,
two (2) members of the Fire Pension Fund Board shall be elected, one for a two
(2) year term and one for a one year term, so that annually thereafter one
member shall be elected for a two (2) year term.
   C.   The City Attorney shall advise and represent the Board in all matters
pertaining to its duties and the management of the fund whenever required.
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.702: CONTRIBUTIONS TO FUND:
   A.   Each member will pay into the fund ten percent (10%) of the following:
      1.   Base pay (including sick leave pay and vacation leave pay taken in
the normal course of employment), not reduced by amounts contributed to a
retirement health savings plan;
      2.   Pay based on length of service (third week pay) and longevity pay;
      3.   Pay for mandatory overtime and annual leave pay that is part of the
member's fixed periodic compensation;
      4.   Performance pay; and
      5.   Vacation leave paid as a lump sum.
   B.   The payment required by subsection A of this section will be made by
the employer by a deduction from the salary paid to the member, and the amount
deducted will be treated as picked up by the employer and as employer
contributions for purposes of section 414(h)(2) of the Internal Revenue Code of
1986, as amended. The employer will pay these employee contributions directly
to the fund and not to the employee. The contributions, although designated as
employee contributions, will be paid by the employer. Employees may not elect
to receive the contributions directly. Employee contributions picked up will be
treated in the same manner as employee contributions made before the date
picked up. All payments will be credited to the pension fund. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.703: BENEFITS, RETURN OF CONTRIBUTIONS, AND VESTED SEPARATION:
   A.   "Eligibility for normal retirement" means that a member has at least
twenty five (25) years of service, has attained the age of fifty (50), and is a
member of the plan established under this part. A member eligible for normal
retirement may separate from service and be paid a monthly benefit equal to
one-half (1/2) of the final monthly value of the amounts specified in
subsections
1.4.702A1 through A3 of this part. Whenever a member who has not reached
eligibility for normal retirement separates from service, the member's total
contributions will be returned to the member (without interest) unless the
member has twenty (20) or more years of service. A member who has twenty (20)
or more years of service, separates from service prior to age fifty (50), and
does not elect to have his or her contributions returned will receive a monthly
vested separation benefit. The monthly vested separation benefit will begin
when the member becomes age fifty (50). The monthly vested separation benefit
will be the lesser of: 1) fifty percent (50%) of the final monthly value of the
amounts specified in subsections
1.4.702A1 through A3 of this part, or 2) two percent (2%) per year of the final
monthly value of the amounts specified in subsections
1.4.702A1 through A3 of this part for each full year of service. A member whose
monthly benefit under this plan does not begin immediately upon separation from
service will not receive the postretirement cash contributions specified in
subsection
1.4.204B of this article.
   B.   In addition to the monthly benefit provided in subsection A of this
section, a member who separates from service after reaching eligibility for
normal retirement may elect to receive: 1) the contributions the member made to
the fund under subsection
1.4.702A of this part for all months beginning after the member reached
eligibility for normal retirement, or 2) a monthly supplemental retirement
benefit of three percent (3%) of the final monthly value of the amounts
specified in subsections
1.4.702A1 through A3 of this part for each full year of service completed after
reaching eligibility for normal retirement, up to six (6) years.
   C.   In addition to the monthly benefits described in subsections A and B of
this section, a member who separates from service will receive a lump sum
payment for performance pay if performance pay was awarded to sworn members for
the previous year. The performance pay will be determined by multiplying the
annualized retirement benefit of the member by a fraction, the numerator of
which is the total performance pay paid to all sworn members for the previous
year and the denominator of which is the total of the values of subsections
1.4.702A1 through A3 of this part paid to all sworn members for the previous
year.
   D.   In addition to the monthly benefits provided in subsections A and B of
this section, a member who separates from service will receive a rank
escalation benefit. The rank escalation benefit will be determined by
multiplying: 1) the sum of the percentages in subsections A and B of this
section by which the member's final monthly value of the amounts specified in
subsections
1.4.702A1 through A3 of this part is multiplied to determine the member's
normal retirement benefit, vested separation benefit and supplemental
retirement benefit, by 2) the increase for the current year over the previous
year of the sum of the monthly values for subsections
1.4.702A1 through A3 of this part for an active sworn member who holds the same
rank the member had at the time the member's retirement benefits began. Once a
monthly rank escalation benefit is awarded, the amount of the monthly benefit
will be a part of the monthly benefit the member receives in subsequent years.
No rank escalation benefit will be awarded or used to increase benefits to the
member for the time prior to the date the member begins receiving a monthly
benefit under subsection A of this section.
   E.   A member who qualifies for death or disability benefits under a plan
administered by the Fire and Police Pension Association of Colorado will not
qualify for a return of contributions or any benefit under this plan. A member
who elects to have his or her contributions returned will not be entitled to
any benefit under this plan. This plan will be construed so that a member
(including a surviving spouse or a child of the member) will not receive more
than one of the following benefits: 1) monthly normal retirement benefit, 2)
monthly vested separation benefit, 3) monthly death benefit under this part, or
4) monthly death or disability benefit under a plan administered by the Fire
and Police Pension Association of Colorado.
   F.   Unless section
1.4.712 of this part applies, all benefits under this section will end on the
date of member's death. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.704: DEFERRED RETIREMENT OPTION PLAN:
   A.   Establishment: An optional benefit known as the deferred retirement
option plan, or DROP, is added to the firefighter's pension plan.
   B.   Eligibility For Participation; Limitations:
      1.   Participation in DROP is an option available to any member of the
plan established under this part who is eligible to retire in accord with
section
1.4.703 of this part.
      2.   A member may participate in DROP only once.
      3.   The duration of a member's participation in the DROP shall not
exceed a total of five (5) years. As a condition precedent to participation in
DROP, the member shall execute an irrevocable agreement with the Firefighter's
Pension Fund Board and the City of Colorado Springs, which agreement shall,
among other items, clearly and unequivocally state that the member must retire
no later than the fifth anniversary of initial participation in DROP. The
member shall also acknowledge that no disbursement of DROP funds can occur
absent the retirement or death of the member.
      4.   If the member's participation in the DROP is interrupted by: a)
military service, b) reduction in work force, or c) job related disability,
upon reestablishment of membership, provided the member has not received any
distribution from the member's DROP account, the member shall be immediately
eligible for resumption of participation for the balance of the five (5) year
maximum. Other than the above described types of interruptions, the five (5)
year period shall continue to run in all other cases.
   C.   Conditions Of Participation; Effects:
      1.   When a member participates in DROP, the member will remain an active
member of the retirement plan, but will earn no additional service credit and
may not purchase service credit.
      2.   When a member participates in DROP, the benefits provided by this
retirement plan and the employee contributions required by section
1.4.702 of this part will be paid into the DROP account of the member and not
to the fund, and there will be no employer contributions paid, on behalf of the
member, into the fund or to the DROP account.
      3.   The deferred retirement option plan assets shall be held in trust
for investment purposes as part of the fire and police members' self-directed
investments fund, subject to such rules as may be adopted for the
administration of the trust. The FPPA Board shall be authorized to charge each
account a reasonable fee for the administration of the DROP.
      4.   The deferred retirement option plan account shall not be subject to
any fees or charges of any kind for any purpose, except as otherwise agreed by
the City and FPPA.
   D.   Payments To Member:
      1.   A member in the DROP who terminates employment or reaches the five
(5) year limit for participation shall become a retiree and shall be entitled
to select one of the following distribution methods:
         a.   Deferral of any payment(s) from the account until a specified
date. If a deferral of payment(s) is selected, the member shall select one of
the following distribution methods. However, all distributions must start no
later than the year in which the member attains the age of seventy and one-half
(701/2).
         b.   A lump sum distribution of the entire account balance.
         c.   Periodic monthly payments with a designated amount until the
balance of the DROP account has been entirely distributed.
         d.   Periodic payments for a designated period of years. FPPA will
calculate the dollar amount of the member's periodic payment, so that the
entire balance in the member's DROP account will have been distributed to the
member by the end of the period selected by the member. This amount will be
recalculated annually during April.
         e.   Initial minimum required distribution. The FPPA will calculate
the dollar amount of the member's periodic payment based on the member's
current DROP account balance. The minimum distribution is based on the member's
life expectancy (and the life expectancy of the member's designated
beneficiary, if applicable).
         f.   Combination of lump sum and periodic payments by designating an
initial lump sum payment of a specified amount and a balance to be paid in a
specified number of monthly payments of a specified dollar amount until the
balance of the DROP account has been entirely distributed to the member.
      2.   Regardless of the form of payment the member chooses, the minimum
distribution amount will be determined and made in accord with Internal Revenue
Code section 401(a)(9) and the regulations thereunder, including the minimum
distribution incidental death benefit requirement. If no selection is made by
the retiree within thirty (30) days of retirement, the lump sum payment method
shall be utilized.
   E.   Payments To Beneficiaries:
      1.   The legal spouse of a member shall be the primary beneficiary of the
DROP account for the purpose of survivor benefits. If a member is not legally
married, the member may elect one or more primary beneficiaries to receive the
balance of the account in the event of the member's death. A member may also
elect one or more contingent beneficiaries who would be eligible to receive the
proceeds of the DROP account in the event that no primary beneficiary survives
the member by at least thirty (30) days.
      2.   The member may change elective beneficiaries as personal
circumstances dictate.
      3.   If a member dies during the period of participation in the DROP plan
and the legal spouse of said member is the beneficiary, at the spouse's option,
the member shall be eligible to receive either: a) a lump sum payment equal to
the account balance plus any accrued interest or b) equal monthly installment
payments from the member's individual DROP account over a period of no more
than ten (10) years. If the beneficiary is other than the spouse of the member
or if no selection is made by the spouse beneficiary within thirty (30) days of
death of the member, the lump sum payment method shall be utilized.
      4.   In the event that the member dies and is not survived by a
designated beneficiary by at least thirty (30) days, the member's estate shall
receive a lump sum payment equal to the member's individual DROP account
balance, plus any accrued interest.
      5.   Payments of DROP account proceeds shall be in addition to other
normal survivor benefits payable to survivors of retirees as provided in this
article.
   F.   Compliance With IRS Requirements: The Board shall take all necessary
steps to ensure that the DROP is administered in full compliance with all
applicable IRS rules, regulations and determinations. For purposes of the
limits of Internal Revenue Code section 415, the DROP is considered a defined
benefit plan to which Internal Revenue Code section 415(b) applies at the time
benefits are paid from the DROP plan. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.705: DIRECT ROLLOVERS:
For distributions made on or after January 1, 1993, a member or beneficiary may
elect, at the time and in the manner prescribed by the Fire Pension Fund Board,
to have any portion of an eligible rollover distribution paid directly to an
eligible retirement plan specified by the member or beneficiary in a direct
rollover. For purposes of applying this section, the following definitions
shall apply:
DISTRIBUTEE: Includes an employee or former employee. In addition, the
employee's or former employee's surviving spouse and the employee's or former
employee's spouse or former spouse who is the alternative payee under a
qualified domestic relations order, as defined in Internal Revenue Code section
414(p), are distributees with regard to the interest of the spouse or former
spouse.
ELIGIBLE RETIREMENT PLAN: An individual retirement account described in
Internal Revenue Code section 408(a), an individual retirement annuity
described in Internal Revenue Code section 408(b), an annuity plan described in
Internal Revenue Code section 403(a) that accepts the distributee's eligible
rollover distribution or a qualified trust described in Internal Revenue Code
section 401(a). However, in the case of an eligible rollover distribution to
the surviving spouse, an eligible retirement plan is an individual retirement
account or individual retirement annuity.
ELIGIBLE ROLLOVER DISTRIBUTION: Any distribution of all or any portion of the
balance to the credit of the distributee, except that an eligible rollover
distribution does not include any distribution that is one of a series of
substantially equal periodic payments (not less frequently than annually) made
for the life (or life expectancy) of the distributee or the joint lives (or
joint life expectancies) of the distributee and the distributee's designated
beneficiary, or for a specified period of ten (10) years or more; any
distribution to the extent the distribution is required under Internal Revenue
Code section 401(a)(9); and the portion of any distribution that is not
includable in gross income.
Effective January 1, 2002, an "eligible retirement plan" shall also mean an
annuity contract described in Internal Revenue Code section 403(b) and an
eligible plan under Internal Revenue Code section 457(b) that is maintained by
a state, political subdivision of a state, or agency or instrumentality of a
state or political subdivision of a state and that agrees separately to account
for amounts transferred into the plan from this plan. The definition of
eligible retirement plan shall also apply in the case of a distribution to a
surviving spouse, or to a spouse or former spouse who is the alternate payee
under a qualified domestic relations order, as defined in Internal Revenue Code
section 414(p).
For distributions on or after January 1, 2002, a portion of distribution shall
not fail to be an eligible rollover distribution merely because the portion
consists of after tax employee contributions that are not includable in gross
income. However, that portion may be paid only to an individual retirement
account or annuity described in section 408(a) or (b) of the Internal Revenue
Code, or to a qualified defined contribution plan described in section 401(a)
or 403(a) of the Internal Revenue Code that agrees separately to account for
the amounts so transferred, including separately accounting for the portion of
the distribution which is includable in gross income and the portion of the
distribution which is not so includable. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.706: EXCLUSIVE BENEFIT RULE:
All contributions made to the firefighter's pension fund shall be used solely
for the exclusive benefit of members and their beneficiaries and to defray
reasonable expenses of the firefighter's pension fund. Forfeitures arising
because of death or termination of employment before a member becomes eligible
for a benefit from the plan or arising for any other reason shall be applied to
reduce the cost of the plan, not to increase the benefits otherwise payable to
members. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.707: INTERNAL REVENUE SERVICE LIMITATIONS:
   A.   Compensation Limits: The compensation taken into account for any
purpose under the firefighter's pension fund shall not exceed the applicable
amount under Internal Revenue Code section 401(a)(17).
   B.   Benefit Limits: The firefighter's pension fund is subject to the
limitations on benefits described in Internal Revenue Code section 415(b) for
governmental fire plans, which limitations are incorporated by this reference.
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.708: LATEST DISTRIBUTION DATE:
Payment of a member's benefit shall commence no later than April 1 of the
calendar year following the later of: a) the calendar year in which the member
attains age seventy and one-half (701/2), or b) the calendar year in which the
member's employment with the Fire Department terminates. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.709: VESTING UPON PLAN TERMINATION:
If the firefighter's pension fund terminates, the rights of all affected
members to benefits accrued to the date of termination, to the extent then
funded, shall be nonforfeitable. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.710: MILITARY SERVICE:
Effective December 12, 1994, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary,
contributions, benefits and service credit with respect to qualified military
service will be provided in accord with Internal Revenue Code section 414(u).
(Ord. 11-18)
1.4.711: RULES AND FORMS:
The Fire Pension Plan Board is authorized to promulgate rules and forms
necessary to administer, interpret and implement this part. (Ord. 11-18)
1.4.712: BENEFITS TO DEPENDENTS:
   A.   Death While Employed As An Officer In The Fire Department:
      1.   If a member of a plan established under this part dies while in
service, and if that member has reached age fifty (50), has twenty five (25)
years of service or more and has a surviving spouse, the surviving spouse will
receive monthly, for the remainder of the spouse's life, two-thirds (2/3) of
the monthly benefit the member would have received at the time of the member's
death had the member been retired as of the date of death and two-thirds (2/3)
of any increase in the monthly benefit the member would have received had the
member been retired as of the date of death.
      2.   If a member of a plan established under this part dies while in
service, and if that member has reached age fifty (50), has twenty five (25)
years of service or more, and has a child or children, each child under age
eighteen (18) (or under age 23 if unmarried and enrolled as a full time student
in an accredited institution of higher learning) will receive, monthly, thirty
dollars ($30.00) if there is a surviving spouse. If there is no surviving
spouse, or after the surviving spouse dies, the child or children as described
above will receive, monthly, the greater of the share of the benefit that the
surviving spouse would have received, prorated among all children described
above, or thirty dollars ($30.00). A benefit paid to a child will cease once
that child no longer meets the criteria described above.
   B.   Death After Benefits Begin:
      1.   If a member of a plan established under this part who is receiving a
monthly benefit dies, the member's surviving spouse will receive monthly, for
the remainder of the spouse's life, two-thirds (2/3) of the benefit the member
would have received.
      2.   If a member of a plan established under this part dies, each child
under age eighteen (18) (or under age 23 if unmarried and enrolled as a full
time student in an accredited institution of higher learning) will receive,
monthly, thirty dollars ($30.00) if there is a surviving spouse. If there is no
surviving spouse, or after the surviving spouse dies, the child or children as
described above will receive, monthly, the greater of the share of the benefit
that would have been paid to the surviving spouse, prorated among all children
described above, or thirty dollars ($30.00). A benefit paid to a child will
cease once that child no longer meets the criteria described above.
   C.   Death Of A Member Eligible For, Or Receiving, Vested Separation
Benefits:
      1.   When a member who is eligible for, or who is receiving, vested
separation benefits dies, the surviving spouse will receive, monthly, a benefit
beginning on the later of the date the member would have been age fifty (50) or
the date of the member's death. The monthly benefit will be two-thirds (2/3) of
the monthly vested separation benefit the member would have received at the
time the member would have been age fifty (50) or, if the member was receiving
monthly vested separation benefits on the date of member's death, two-thirds
(2/3) of the monthly vested separation benefit the member was receiving. The
surviving spouse will also receive, monthly, two-thirds (2/3) of any rank
escalation benefit the member would have received. The monthly benefit paid to
the surviving spouse will terminate on the date of death of the surviving
spouse.
      2.   When a member who is eligible for, or who is receiving, monthly
vested separation benefits dies and has a child or children, each child under
age eighteen (18) (or under age 23 if unmarried and enrolled as a full time
student in an accredited institution of higher learning) will receive, monthly,
thirty dollars ($30.00) if there is a surviving spouse. If there is no
surviving spouse, or after the surviving spouse dies, the child or children as
described above will receive, monthly, the greater of the share of the benefit
the surviving spouse would have received, prorated among all children described
above, or thirty dollars ($30.00). A benefit paid to a child will cease once
that child no longer meets the criteria described above. (Ord. 11-18)

1.5.101: DEFINITIONS:
APPROPRIATION: The authorization granted in the annual appropriation ordinance
for the funds of the City.
BUDGET: The classification and allocation of an estimate of revenues and
expenditures within each of the various accounts and funds.
DEPARTMENT: Any department, division, office or agency of the City as may be
designated, from time to time, by the Mayor, the Utilities Executive Director
or City Council.
SPECIAL FUND: Any special fund of the City as may be designated, from time to
time, by the Mayor or City Council. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.102: BUDGET; CREATION OF ACCOUNTS 1 :
After the annual budget identifying appropriation departments is approved by
the City Council, the Chief Financial Officer shall set up the necessary
accounts and assign account numbers to specific items in the City budget to be
designated as appropriation accounts. The Chief Financial Officer shall set up
the fund accounts as set forth in the City budget and shall pay only charges of
the nature classified. (Ord. 11-18; Ord. 17-86)
 
Notes
1 2. See City Charter section 7-30.
1.5.103: APPROPRIATION AND TAX LEVY ORDINANCE; AMENDMENT:
   A.   From time to time, the Mayor may recommend the revision and amendments
to the City appropriation ordinance in order to reflect corrections of revenues
and expenditures, and shall transmit the recommendation to the Council that an
amendment or amendments to the annual appropriation ordinance be adopted 1 .
The City Council shall consider the recommendations and may adopt the same with
or without amendment.
   B.   In amending the appropriation ordinance, the City Council may reduce or
omit any item or add or increase any item 2 . By ordinance, the Council may
amend the annual tax levy and appropriation ordinances to reflect corrections
of revenue and expenditures to accord with actual fact. Also, in the event of
casualty, accident or unforeseen contingency, the City Council may by ordinance
make a new or special appropriation. (Ord. 11-18)
 
Notes
1 1. City Council annually appropriates by ordinance the sums contained in the
  budget. See City Charter section 7-50.
  2. See City Charter subsection 7-30(a). No amendment to the budget may
2 increase authorized expenditures to an amount greater than the total of
  estimated income.
1.5.104: TRANSFER OF FUNDS WITHIN APPROPRIATION DEPARTMENTS OR SPECIAL FUNDS:
At any time, the Mayor may authorize the Chief Financial Officer to transfer
any unexpended City appropriation account balance or portion from one account
number or classification of expenditure to another within the same
appropriation department or special fund. (Ord. 11-18; Ord. 17-86)
1.5.105: TRANSFER OF FUNDS BETWEEN APPROPRIATION DEPARTMENTS OR SPECIAL FUNDS:
By resolution, the City Council may authorize the Mayor to transfer any
unexpended City appropriation account balance or portion, or transfer funds
from one appropriation department to another within the same fund. (Ord. 11-18;
Ord. 17-86)
1.5.106: TRANSFER OF FUNDS FROM CONTINGENCY ACCOUNT:
At any time, the Mayor may authorize the Chief Financial Officer to transfer
any unexpended balance or portion from the General Fund contingency account to
another group, department or special fund. The Mayor shall report each transfer
from the General Fund contingency account to the City Council not later than
the first regular Council meeting of the calendar month following the date of
the transfer, together with a statement of the balance remaining in General
Fund contingency account following the transfer. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.107: PROJECTS; ABANDONMENT OR PARTIAL ABANDONMENT:
At any time, the Mayor may recommend the abandonment or partial abandonment of
a City project. The recommendation shall be accompanied by a detailed
description of the reduction in scope or partial abandonment. Upon receipt of
the recommendation and supporting data, the City Council by resolution may
abandon or partially abandon any project. Council may authorize the transfer of
the funds for the abandoned or partially abandoned project to another project
account or to the undesignated and unappropriated reserves of the City. (Ord.
11-18; Ord. 17-79)
1.5.108: SPECIAL PROJECTS; TRANSFER OF FUNDS:
The Mayor may transfer appropriation accounts or portions from one special
project to another only after a project has been completed. In the case of
special projects that have been abandoned or partially abandoned pursuant to
section
1.5.107 of this part, the Mayor may transfer City appropriation accounts or
portions from one project to another only upon approval of the transfer by the
City Council. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.109: SPECIAL PROJECTS; NONLAPSE OF APPROPRIATIONS:
   A.   Appropriations for special projects of the various funds included in
the budget shall not lapse until the purpose for which the appropriation was
made has been accomplished or abandoned.
   B.   Any unexpended funds which were appropriated for a special project
which has been completed or abandoned and which have not been transferred
pursuant to section
1.5.108 of this part shall lapse back to the originating fund for
reappropriation by ordinance. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.110: FILING OF INVENTORIES:
The Mayor shall cause an account of all capital items of equipment, real
estate, buildings and permanent installations owned by the City. Accounting
shall comply with rules and regulations promulgated by the Mayor in accord with
generally accepted accounting principles. (Ord. 11-18)

USING AGENCY: Includes any department, division, agency, commission, office or
other unit of the City government using supplies or procuring contractual
services as provided in this part. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.203: ESTABLISHMENT OF PURCHASING OFFICE 1 :
There is hereby established a Purchasing Office. (Ord. 11-18)
 
Notes

  1.2.312  of this chapter.
1.5.204: PURCHASING MANAGER:
   A.   Purchasing Authority: The Manager shall have the power and duty to
purchase or contract for all supplies, services, and construction needed for
any City function or by any using agency that derives its support wholly or in
part from the City, in accord with the City of Colorado Springs Procurement
Rules and Regulations ("Rules and Regulations") prescribed and approved by the
City Council.
   B.   Other Powers And Duties: In addition to purchasing authority and in
addition to any other powers and duties conferred by this part, the Manager
shall:
      1.   Minimum Expenditure: Act to procure for the City the highest quality
in supplies and contractual services at least expense to the City;
      2.   Open Competition: Discourage uniform bidding and endeavor to obtain
as full and open competition as possible on all purchases and sales;
      3.   Rules And Regulations: The Manager may recommend changes to the
Rules and Regulations to the Mayor. The Mayor or the Mayor's designee shall
submit proposed changes to the Rules and Regulations in writing to all City
Council members. Within ten (10) business days of the submission to Council,
any Council Member may request that the proposed changes be scheduled for
discussion at an informal City Council meeting. After City Council has
discussed the proposed changes Council may accept the changes or request
modifications be made. If Council accepts, the proposed changes shall
automatically become effective. If Council requests modifications, the Mayor
shall reconsider the proposed change and resubmit any modifications to Council.
Any resubmitted modifications shall follow the same procedure as outlined
above. Should no City Council Member request that the proposed changes be
scheduled for discussion, the proposed changes shall automatically become
effective;
      4.   Purchasing Analysis: Keep informed of current developments in the
field of purchasing, prices, market conditions and new products and secure for
the City the benefits of research performed in the field of purchasing by other
governmental jurisdictions, national technical societies, trade associations
having national recognition, and private businesses and organizations;
      5.   Forms: Prescribe and maintain forms reasonably necessary to the
operation and administration of this part;
      6.   Standard Nomenclature: Prepare and adopt a standard purchasing
nomenclature for using agencies and suppliers;
      7.   Vendors' Database: Prepare, adopt and maintain a vendors' database,
that will allow vendors to register and receive automated notifications
electronically for invitation of bids and requests for proposals via the City's
website;
      8.   Bulk Purchases: Explore the possibilities of buying "in bulk" so as
to take full advantage of discounts;
      9.   Federal Tax Exemptions: Act so as to procure for the City all
Federal tax exemptions to which it is entitled;
      10.   Cooperation With Other City Departments: Cooperate with other City
departments so as to secure for the City the maximum efficiency in budgeting
and accounting; and
      11.   Disqualification Of Bidders: Have the authority to declare as
irresponsible bidders vendors who default on their quotations, and to
disqualify the vendors from receiving any business from the City for a stated
period of time. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.205: COMPETITIVE BIDDING REQUIRED:
All purchases of and contracts for supplies and services, and all sales of
personal property which has become obsolete and unusable shall, except as
otherwise specifically provided in this part, be based whenever possible on
competitive bids. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.206: FORMAL BIDDING PROCEDURE:
   A.   The provisions of this section shall not apply to the purchase of
justified sole source items. Purchases of supplies, materials, equipment and
services having an estimated value of less than the formal competition
threshold specified in the City Procurement Rules and Regulations may be made
using informal bidding procedures in accord with the procurement rules and
regulations.
   B.   Notice inviting bids or proposals shall be published and advertised in
accord with the City Procurement Rules and Regulations. Notice shall include a
general description of the articles to be purchased or sold, a statement as to
where solicitation documents may be obtained, and the time and place where the
bids will be opened or proposals received.
   C.   Each bid or proposal shall be submitted in accord with the instructions
in the solicitation to the Manager in a sealed envelope. All bids shall be
opened in public at the time and place specified in the solicitation, and a
tabulation of all bids received posted for public inspection on the City's
website. All proposals shall be received by the time and date specified in the
request for proposal. Information regarding the names and number of proposals
received will not be made known to the public until an award is announced, in
accord with the City Procurement Rules and Regulations.
   D.   The Manager may reject all bids, under the conditions defined in the
City's Procurement Rules and Regulations. The Manager shall not accept the bid
or proposal of any contractor who is currently suspended or debarred from doing
business with the City as per the City Procurement Rules and Regulations.
All bids and proposals shall be handled, reviewed and evaluated, and any bid
accepted or awarded shall be in strict accord with the City Procurement Rules
and Regulations. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.207: SUFFICIENCY OF FUNDS:
Except in cases of an emergency, the Manager shall not issue any order for
delivery on a contract or open market purchase until the proper officer, group
or department director or manager certifies, after preaudit, that there is to
the credit of the using agency concerned a sufficient appropriation balance, in
excess of all unpaid obligations, to defray the cost of the contract or open
market purchase. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.208: COOPERATIVE PURCHASING:
The Manager shall have the authority to join with other units of government in
cooperative purchasing plans when the best interests of the City would be
served. (Ord. 11-18)
1.5.209: EXCLUSIONS 1 :
Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, the provisions of this part
shall not be applicable to the leasing, rental, acquisition or disposition of
real property, or to attorney retention contracts. (Ord. 11-18)

PART 3 DISBURSEMENTS 1
SECTION:
1.5.301: Disbursement Vouchers Required
1.5.302: Drawing Of Checks; Procedures
 
Notes
1 1. Prior ordinance history: 1968 Code §3-3g; Ord. 76-54; Ord. 01-42.
1.5.301: DISBURSEMENT VOUCHERS REQUIRED:
No City funds or monies shall be expended or disbursed except by vouchers
approved by the Chief Financial Officer or the officer's designee. Minor cash
disbursements from a petty cash fund to be established by vouchers drawn to
that account and approved by the Chief Financial Officer or the officer's
designee may be made. The Chief Financial Officer may designate a person to
approve the vouchers in the name of the officer, and when so approved, the
vouchers shall be to all effects and purposes as if approved by the officer.
(Ord. 11-18)
1.5.302: DRAWING OF CHECKS; PROCEDURES:
The Mayor and the Chief Financial Officer shall sign all checks drawn upon
accounts of the City.
   A.   Each check shall state the particular fund or appropriation to which it
is chargeable and the person to whom payable.
   B.   It shall be the duty of the Chief Financial Officer to see that proper
authority has been granted by ordinance, contract, Council action or otherwise
for the payment of all amounts for which checks are issued and that no check
exceeds the appropriation upon which it is drawn.
   C.   The department, division, office or agency director or manager or City
Council approving each item shall ensure that the labor has been performed, the
goods, wares and merchandise involved have been received and that the price is
proper. (Ord. 11-18)
PART 4 CLAIMS AND GIFTS 1
SECTION:
1.5.401: Claims Against The City
1.5.402: Conditions Of Gifts; Acceptance
1.5.403: Designation Of Donee
